title: Scrotal Pain
hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with unilateral scrotal pain of gradual onset, swelling, tenderness, and erythema. Pain may radiate to lower abdomen. Prehn's sign: pain improves with scrotal elevation (distinguishes from testicular torsion — no relief with elevation, acute onset). Caused by ascending infection: sexually active young men → Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Older men or post-instrumentation → E. coli, enteric organisms. Diagnosis: UA (pyuria), urine culture, CT/GC NAAT. Scrotal ultrasound with Doppler if torsion suspected (increased flow in epididymitis, decreased/absent in torsion). Treatment: CT/GC → ceftriaxone 250mg IM once + doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 10d. Enteric → levofloxacin x 10d. Scrotal elevation, NSAIDs, ice. Treat sexual partners.
